To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chromaffin cells from the adrenal gland of mice have resting potential and action potentials and that the electrical properties of the cells are similar to those reported in chromaffin cell cultures.
resting membrane potential of chromaffin cell is -54.3 +/-8.8 m V and that the membrane is electrically excitable and responds to acetylcholine.
chromaffin cells are electrically coupled and that the resting potential of chromaffin cell is determined by the K+ equilibrium potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical properties of adrenal chromaffin cells.
the membrane properties of chromaffin cell and the role of the adrenal medulla in the sympathetic nervous system.
the membrane potential of chromaffin cell and their response to acetylcholine in intact adrenal gland of the adult mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the membrane properties of medullary cells in intact mouse adrenal glands are similar to those of cells in culture and in isolation.
the electrical activity of chromaffin cell is regulated by the extracellular K+, Na+ and ACh.
the chromaffin system of the mouse adrenal gland behaves as if it were a functional syncytium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
electrical activity in mouse chromaffin cells is not essential for catecholamine secretion and that electrical activity is regulated by the extracellular K+ concentration.

electrical activity is present in the adrenal medullary chromatin cells of the mouse and that this activity is regulated by extracellular [K+], tetrodotoxim, and Ba2+, and that it is also regulated by ACh via muscarinic receptors.
the chromaffin system in situ is electrically coupled, and that the membrane potential of chromaffin cell is regulated by the activity of voltage-dependent K+ channels and by muscarinic receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chromaffin cells are electrically coupled and that this coupling may be important for the coordinated release of catecholamines from the chromaffin granules.
electrical activity of chromaffin cell can be studied in situ.
the electrical activity of chromaffin cell can be recorded in intact adrenal glands, which allows us to study the effects of hormones and neurotransmitters on electrical activity.
